options: A detailed lecture covering every option
Medical terms to keep the facts precise
Written materials and a few key points
Waiting until next year to discuss it
questions.explain: Anxiety limits how much a person can absorb, so focusing on a few essentials and giving written materials to review later helps. The patient can bring questions back to the provider.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Patient Care Coordination and Education (preventive care)
questions.q: Which federal agency publishes the routine immunization schedules commonly used in US practices?
questions.explain: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention publishes the child, adolescent and adult immunization schedules. The FDA licenses vaccines, OSHA regulates workplace safety and CMS runs Medicare and Medicaid.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Patient Care Coordination and Education (community resources)
questions.q: A caregiver of a patient with dementia says she is exhausted. Which resource could the MA suggest per office protocol?
options: A caregiver support or respite program
A new prescription for the caregiver from the MA
An urgent care visit for the patient
A transfer of the patient's records
questions.explain: Respite care and caregiver support groups give family caregivers rest and help. Prescribing is outside the MA's scope, and the MA informs the provider about caregiver strain.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (scheduling)
questions.q: Which scheduling method books several patients at the start of each hour to be seen in order of arrival?
questions.explain: Wave scheduling books several patients at the top of the hour and sees them as they arrive, absorbing late arrivals. Stream scheduling gives each patient an individual time, and open hours use no appointments.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (scheduling)
questions.q: Which scheduling method gives each patient an individual appointment time for a set length of time?
questions.explain: Stream, or time-specified, scheduling assigns each patient a specific time based on the expected length of the visit. It is the most common method in medical offices.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (scheduling)
questions.q: What does establishing the matrix of an appointment schedule mean?
options: Booking the most urgent patients first each morning
Printing the schedule for the front desk
Blocking times when providers are unavailable
questions.explain: The matrix blocks out times when appointments cannot be booked, such as meetings, hospital rounds or lunch, before patients are scheduled. This prevents booking into unavailable time.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (scheduling)
questions.q: A patient misses an appointment without calling. What should be done?
options: Delete the appointment from the system
Charge the patient's card without notice
Remove the patient from the practice
Document the no-show per office policy
questions.explain: No-shows are documented in the patient's record and schedule because they may matter legally and for follow-up. Fees or dismissal follow written office policy, not an on-the-spot decision.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (scheduling)
questions.q: Why are new patient appointments usually longer than established patient follow-ups?
options: New patients need a full history and registration
New patients pay higher copays for longer visits
Established patients do not need vital signs
Providers see new patients only once a year
questions.explain: A first visit requires a complete history, registration and a more thorough examination. Established patients already have records on file, so follow-ups can be shorter.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (EHR)
questions.q: What is an advantage of an electronic health record over a paper chart?
options: It never requires a password or login to open
Several authorized users can view it at once
It allows staff to delete old entries
It removes the need for documentation
questions.explain: An EHR can be accessed by several authorized users at the same time and supports legibility, alerts and data sharing. It still requires secure logins and complete documentation.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (EHR)
questions.q: An MA notices an error in an entry in the electronic health record. How should it be corrected?
options: Make a dated correction that keeps the original visible
Delete the whole entry and then type the new one over it
Ask a coworker to edit it under their login
Leave it because EHR entries cannot change
questions.explain: Corrections follow the office procedure, adding a dated correction or addendum under the user's own login while the original remains in the audit trail. Deleting entries or using another person's login is improper.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (EHR)
questions.q: What does the audit trail in an electronic health record show?
options: Who accessed or changed a record and when
How much the patient owes the practice today
The list of the patient's medications
questions.explain: An audit trail logs each user who views, creates or changes information and the time it happened. It supports HIPAA security and helps detect inappropriate access.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (records management)
questions.q: Using standard alphabetic filing rules, which name is filed first?
questions.explain: Filing compares last names unit by unit, and nothing comes before something, so Brown precedes Browne and Brownell. Within the Brown entries, Anna precedes Anne.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (records management)
questions.q: In a SOAP progress note, where is the patient's measured blood pressure recorded?
questions.explain: The objective section holds measurable findings such as vital signs and exam results. Subjective is what the patient reports, assessment is the provider's diagnosis or impression, and plan is the treatment.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (front desk)
questions.q: Why does the front desk copy both sides of a patient's insurance card?
options: The back shows the patient's diagnosis codes and history
The back replaces the need for a photo ID
The back lists claims addresses and phone numbers
The back lists the deductible already met
questions.explain: The front shows identifiers such as the member ID and group number, while the back often lists claims mailing addresses and phone numbers for verification. Neither side lists diagnoses.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (insurance basics)
questions.q: Why is a patient's insurance eligibility checked before the visit?
options: To decide which diagnosis code to report on the claim
To get the patient's medical history
To find out the patient's employer
To confirm coverage is active and note benefits
questions.explain: Verifying eligibility confirms that the policy is active and identifies copays, deductibles and authorization needs, which reduces claim denials and surprises for the patient.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (prior authorization)
questions.q: In insurance billing, what is prior authorization?
options: A provider note written after the service is complete
Patient consent to share records with family
A referral from one specialist to another
Insurer approval before certain services are given
questions.explain: Some plans require approval before certain tests, procedures or medications for the service to be covered. Without it, the claim may be denied even though the service was medically necessary.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (insurance basics)
questions.q: Medicare Part B mainly helps pay for which services?
options: Long-term custodial care in nursing homes
questions.explain: Part B covers physician services, outpatient care and preventive services. Part A covers inpatient hospital care, Part D covers prescription drugs, and Medicare generally does not cover long-term custodial care.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (insurance basics)
questions.q: Which program is jointly funded by the federal government and the states for people with limited income and resources?
questions.explain: Medicaid is a joint federal and state program, with eligibility and benefits that vary by state. Medicare is federal coverage mainly for people 65 and older or with certain disabilities.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (insurance basics)
questions.q: A patient was injured on the job. Which coverage is usually billed for the related care?
questions.explain: Work-related injuries and illnesses are usually billed to the employer's workers' compensation carrier, using the claim number for that injury, rather than to the patient's health plan.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (insurance basics)
questions.q: A patient belongs to an HMO plan and wants to see a dermatologist. What is usually required first?
options: A letter from the patient's employer approving the visit
A referral from the primary care provider
A paper claim filed in advance
Payment of the full fee upfront
questions.explain: HMOs usually require the primary care provider to act as gatekeeper and issue a referral before specialist care is covered. Visits without a required referral may be denied.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (front desk)
questions.q: Which sign-in practice protects patient privacy at the front desk?
options: A sign-in sheet listing each patient's diagnosis
Calling out each patient's full name and complaint
Leaving the day's schedule face up on the counter
A sign-in that does not show the reason for visit
questions.explain: Sign-in methods should limit what other patients can see, such as names only or electronic check-in. Displaying diagnoses or reasons for visits discloses more information than necessary.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (front desk)
questions.q: Which information is gathered on a new patient registration form?
options: The provider's diagnosis and treatment plan
The office's fee schedule and contracts
questions.explain: Registration collects name, address, date of birth, contact details, insurance information, responsible party and emergency contact. Clinical information is recorded during the visit.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (records management)
questions.q: What is a tickler file used for?
options: Tracking supplies that are out of stock
Reminders of actions due on future dates
questions.explain: A tickler file, paper or electronic, is organized by date to remind staff of upcoming tasks such as recall appointments, follow-up calls or renewals.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (EHR)
questions.q: Which practice protects EHR security?
options: Sharing a login with a trusted coworker on the same shift
Writing the password on the monitor
Logging off when stepping away from the station
Leaving a record open for the next user
questions.explain: Each user must have a unique login and log off or lock the screen when leaving, so all access is traceable and unauthorized viewing is prevented. Shared passwords defeat the audit trail.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (scheduling)
questions.q: A patient calls to reschedule. What should the MA do with the original appointment?
options: Leave it so the slot stays reserved just in case
Cancel it in the system and note the change
Book the new time and keep both
Erase it with no record of the change
questions.explain: The original appointment is canceled or rescheduled in the system with a note, freeing the slot for others while keeping a record. Leaving duplicate appointments causes confusion and false no-shows.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Administrative Assisting (records management)
questions.q: How are medical records commonly organized in a problem-oriented medical record?
options: By the date of each insurance payment
By the alphabet of the provider's name
By the color of the folder used
By the patient's list of health problems
questions.explain: A problem-oriented record organizes information around a numbered problem list, with progress notes often written in SOAP format for each problem. A source-oriented record groups information by its source.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (therapeutic communication)
questions.q: Which question to a patient is open-ended?
options: How have you been sleeping lately?
Did you sleep well last night?
questions.explain: Open-ended questions invite the patient to answer in their own words and share more detail. Questions that can be answered yes or no are closed-ended and are useful for confirming specific facts.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (therapeutic communication)
questions.q: A patient says, "I'm really worried about this biopsy." Which response uses reflection?
options: You are worried about the biopsy.
You should not worry so much.
Most biopsies are nothing at all.
questions.explain: Reflection restates the patient's feeling so they feel heard and can say more. Reassurance that everything will be fine is a barrier because it dismisses the concern and may be false.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (nonverbal communication)
questions.q: Which nonverbal behavior shows attentive listening?
options: Typing while the patient is speaking
Facing the patient with appropriate eye contact
Standing in the doorway with arms crossed
Looking at the clock during the talk
questions.explain: Facing the patient, keeping an open posture and making culturally appropriate eye contact show attention. Typing without looking up, crossed arms or watching the clock signal disinterest.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (therapeutic communication)
questions.q: Which response is a barrier to therapeutic communication?
options: Allowing a brief period of silence
questions.explain: False reassurance dismisses the patient's feelings and may not be true. Asking for more information, restating and silence are therapeutic techniques that encourage the patient to share.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (telephone)
questions.q: How should the MA answer the office telephone?
options: Say hello and wait for the caller to speak
Answer with only the provider's name
Greet, give the office name and own name
Put the caller on hold right away
questions.explain: A professional greeting identifies the office and the staff member and offers help. Placing a caller on hold before they can speak could delay an emergency.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (telephone)
questions.q: Before placing a caller on hold, what should the MA do?
options: Ask permission and wait for a reply
Place the call on hold without a word
Tell the caller to call back later
Transfer the call to any open line
questions.explain: Asking whether the caller can hold, and waiting for the answer, is courteous and lets the MA catch emergencies. The caller should be checked on regularly if the hold lasts.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (telephone screening)
questions.q: A caller reports crushing chest pain and sweating. What should the MA do?
options: Tell the caller to hang up and call 911 now
Take a message for the provider to return
Advise the caller to rest and call tomorrow
questions.explain: Chest pain with sweating can signal a heart attack. Office protocols direct callers with emergency symptoms to call 911 immediately, and the MA then informs the provider and documents the call.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (difficult situations)
questions.q: A patient is upset about waiting 45 minutes past the appointment time. What is the best response?
options: Acknowledge the wait and give an update
Explain that every patient waits this long
Ignore the comment and keep working
Say the provider is not to blame
questions.explain: Acknowledging feelings, apologizing for the delay and offering an estimate or options often defuse frustration. Arguing or ignoring the patient tends to escalate the situation.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (telephone)
questions.q: When taking a telephone message, which information is essential?
options: Only the caller's first name and general reason
Only the time and the message topic
Name, callback number, reason, date and time
The caller's insurance plan and copay
questions.explain: A complete message includes the caller's full name, the patient's name if different, a callback number, the reason for the call, the date and time, and the initials of the person taking it.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (cultural sensitivity)
questions.q: A patient wants a family elder involved in health decisions, as is customary in her culture. How should the MA respond?
options: Insist that only the patient can be present in the room
Tell the elder to wait outside the building
Respect the preference and follow privacy rules
Assume the elder will make every decision
questions.explain: Respecting cultural preferences builds trust. The patient decides who participates, so the MA follows the patient's wishes and HIPAA procedures for sharing information with family.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (cultural sensitivity)
questions.q: Why should a patient's young child generally not be used as a medical interpreter?
options: Accuracy, privacy and the child's well-being suffer
Children cannot speak two languages fluently at that age
Children are not allowed in medical offices
Children always change the provider's words
questions.explain: Children may not know medical terms, may leave out sensitive details and can be burdened by hearing serious information. A qualified medical interpreter protects accuracy and confidentiality.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (professional behavior)
questions.q: Which behavior best reflects professionalism in a medical office?
options: Using a phone for personal texts at the desk
Arriving on time and ready for the shift
Wearing strong perfume for a fresh image
questions.explain: Punctuality, preparation and respectful conduct are core professional behaviors. Personal phone use at the desk, gossip and strong scents can distract, offend or affect patients with sensitivities.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (electronic communication)
questions.q: A patient portal message describes new severe shortness of breath. What should the MA do?
options: Reply within the usual three business days
Archive the message until the next visit
Answer with general advice from the internet
Act at once per protocol and alert the provider
questions.explain: Messages describing urgent symptoms need immediate action under the office protocol, which may include advising emergency care and notifying the provider right away. Routine response times do not apply.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (therapeutic communication)
questions.q: Which statement to a struggling patient shows empathy?
options: I feel so sorry for you right now.
You should be grateful it is not worse.
It sounds like this has been hard for you.
I know exactly how you feel about it.
questions.explain: Empathy recognizes and reflects the other person's feelings without taking them on. Sympathy expresses pity, minimizing invalidates the feeling, and claiming to know exactly how someone feels can seem dismissive.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (communication across the life span)
questions.q: Before a minor procedure on a young child, which approach is best?
options: Medical terms so the child learns them
Promising that nothing will hurt at all
Simple, honest words at the child's eye level
Talking only to the parent, not the child
questions.explain: Young children understand simple, honest explanations given at their level. Promising that something will not hurt damages trust when it does, and children should be included in the conversation.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (telephone)
questions.q: A patient calls asking for a prescription refill. What should the MA do?
options: Approve the refill because it is a routine request
Tell the patient to stop the medication
Call the pharmacy with a new dose
Take the details and route them per protocol
questions.explain: The MA records the medication, dose, pharmacy and patient information and forwards the request according to office protocol for provider authorization. MAs do not independently approve or change prescriptions.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (therapeutic communication)
questions.q: What is the purpose of a brief silence during a conversation with a patient?
options: It shows the MA is too busy to talk at the moment
It signals that the visit is finished
It gives the patient time to think and share
It lets the MA avoid hard topics
questions.explain: Purposeful silence gives the patient time to collect thoughts and often encourages them to say more. It is a therapeutic technique, not a sign of disinterest.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (therapeutic communication)
questions.q: A patient says, "I just feel funny." Which response seeks clarification?
options: I am sure it is nothing to worry about.
Lots of people feel that way at times.
Let's move on to your medications.
Can you tell me what you mean by funny?
questions.explain: Clarification asks the patient to explain a vague statement so the MA can document it accurately. Reassurance and changing the subject block the information needed.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Communication and Customer Service (nonverbal communication)
questions.q: A patient says "I'm fine" while frowning and guarding the left arm. How should the MA interpret this?
options: The frowning is not worth noting
Words and body language do not match
questions.explain: When verbal and nonverbal messages are incongruent, the nonverbal message is often more accurate. The MA gently explores the discrepancy and documents objective observations without judging the patient.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (HIPAA)
questions.q: Which situation is most likely a HIPAA privacy violation?
options: Faxing records to a verified referral office
Sharing results with the treating provider
Discussing test results in the waiting room
questions.explain: Discussing protected health information where others can hear is an avoidable disclosure. Sharing information with other providers for treatment is permitted, and verifying identity protects privacy.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (HIPAA)
questions.q: A patient's employer calls to ask why the patient was seen today. What should the MA do?
options: Decline without the patient's written authorization
Give the diagnosis because the employer pays the premium
Confirm only the diagnosis code over the phone
Read the visit note to the employer
questions.explain: Employers are not entitled to a patient's health information without the patient's written authorization, except in specific situations such as some workers' compensation claims. The MA politely declines.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (consent)
questions.q: In which situation does implied consent apply?
options: A patient signs a surgical consent form
A patient states a refusal of an injection
A patient asks questions about a procedure
An unconscious patient needs emergency care
questions.explain: In an emergency, consent is implied because a reasonable person would agree to life-saving treatment if able. A signed form is expressed consent, and a stated refusal must be respected.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (consent)
questions.q: Before a minor office surgery, who is responsible for explaining the risks, benefits and alternatives for informed consent?
options: The medical assistant who roomed the patient at intake
questions.explain: The provider performing the procedure explains the risks, benefits and alternatives and answers questions. The MA may witness the signature but does not provide the explanation.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (scope of practice)
questions.q: Which task is outside a medical assistant's scope of practice?
options: Measuring and recording vital signs at intake
Interpreting test results for a patient
questions.explain: Diagnosing and interpreting results require a licensed provider. Vital signs, scheduling and specimen collection are routine MA tasks, subject to state law and employer policy.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (advance directives)
questions.q: What does a durable power of attorney for health care do?
options: Names a person to make care decisions for the patient
Lists the patient's current medications and doses
Transfers the patient's property after death
Grants the provider control of the patient's finances
questions.explain: A durable power of attorney for health care designates an agent to make medical decisions when the patient cannot. It does not handle property, which is covered by other documents.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (advance directives)
questions.q: What does a living will describe?
options: How the patient's property and savings are divided at death
The patient's wishes about life-sustaining treatment
The patient's list of known drug allergies
questions.explain: A living will is an advance directive stating which life-sustaining treatments the patient wants or refuses if unable to communicate. A will that divides property is a separate legal document.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (mandatory reporting)
questions.q: During a visit, an MA notices injuries on a child that appear to be from abuse. What should the MA do?
options: Make sure it is reported as law and policy require
Ignore it unless the child or parent says something about it
Confront the parent in the exam room
Post a description on social media
questions.explain: Health care workers are mandated reporters of suspected child abuse. The MA informs the provider and follows office policy so the report reaches the proper authorities, and documents objective findings.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (negligence)
questions.q: Which elements, often called the four Ds, must be proven in a negligence lawsuit?
options: Duty, dereliction, direct cause and damages
questions.explain: The plaintiff must show the provider had a duty, breached it through dereliction, that the breach directly caused harm, and that damages resulted. All four must be present.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (liability)
questions.q: Which legal doctrine holds an employer responsible for the acts of employees within the scope of their jobs?
questions.explain: Respondeat superior, meaning let the master answer, makes employers liable for employees' acts within the scope of employment. Res ipsa loquitur means the thing speaks for itself.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (patient rights)
questions.q: Under HIPAA, a patient asks for a copy of her own medical records. Which statement is generally true?
options: The provider owns the records and can refuse
She may only view them with a lawyer present
She has a right to access and copies of them
She must give a reason for every request
questions.explain: HIPAA gives patients a right to access and obtain copies of their records, with limited exceptions. A reasonable cost-based fee may apply, and no reason for the request is required.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (ethics)
questions.q: A competent adult declines a recommended flu vaccine after hearing the benefits. Which ethical principle supports honoring the decision?
questions.explain: Autonomy is respect for a competent patient's right to make informed decisions, including refusing care. Beneficence means acting for the patient's good, and justice means fair treatment.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (liability)
questions.q: A provider gives a procedure that a patient clearly refused. What could this be considered?
questions.explain: Battery is unauthorized touching, which includes treatment given without consent. Slander and libel are spoken and written defamation, and abandonment is ending care without proper notice.

questions.ref: NHA CCMA test plan, Medical Law and Ethics (HIPAA)
questions.q: An unencrypted laptop with patient information is lost. What should the MA do?
options: Report it right away to the privacy officer
Wait a week to see if the laptop turns up again
Replace it quietly and tell no one
Post a lost item notice with patient names
questions.explain: Loss of unsecured protected health information may be a breach, so it is reported immediately to the privacy or security officer, who handles assessment and any required notifications.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (coding)
questions.q: Which code set reports the procedures and services a physician performs?
questions.explain: Current Procedural Terminology codes describe procedures and services. ICD-10-CM codes describe diagnoses, NDC numbers identify drug products and the DSM classifies mental disorders.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (coding)
questions.q: Which code set reports a patient's diagnoses on outpatient claims?
questions.explain: ICD-10-CM is used to report diagnoses, symptoms and reasons for encounters. CPT and HCPCS Level II report procedures, services and supplies, and CDT codes are for dental procedures.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (coding)
questions.q: Which code set reports items such as durable medical equipment, supplies and ambulance services?
questions.explain: HCPCS Level II alphanumeric codes cover products, supplies, equipment and services not in CPT. ICD-10-PCS codes inpatient hospital procedures, and CPT Category III covers emerging technology.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (coding)
questions.q: On a claim, how does the diagnosis code relate to the procedure code?
options: It sets the dollar amount the insurer will pay for it
It shows where the patient lives
It supports the medical necessity of the service
questions.explain: The diagnosis code explains why the service was performed, showing medical necessity. Claims whose diagnoses do not support the procedure may be denied.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (claim forms)
questions.q: Which claim form is used to bill professional services from a physician office?
questions.explain: The CMS-1500, or its electronic equivalent, is used for professional services by physicians and other practitioners. The UB-04 is for institutional claims from hospitals and facilities.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (claim forms)
questions.q: Which claim form do hospitals use for institutional services?
questions.explain: The UB-04, also known as CMS-1450, is used for institutional billing by hospitals and other facilities. W-9 and I-9 are tax and employment forms unrelated to claims.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (insurance terms)
questions.q: In health insurance, what is a deductible?
options: A fixed fee paid by the patient at each office visit
The monthly cost of keeping the policy
The amount the patient pays before the plan pays
The percentage the plan pays after costs
questions.explain: A deductible is the amount the insured must pay for covered services each benefit period before the plan begins paying. The fixed visit fee is a copayment, and the monthly cost is the premium.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (insurance terms)
questions.q: In health insurance, what is a copayment?
options: A percentage of the bill after the deductible
The total yearly limit on patient costs
A fixed amount paid for a covered service
The monthly payment that keeps the plan
questions.explain: A copayment is a set dollar amount paid for a service such as an office visit. A percentage split after the deductible is coinsurance, and the monthly payment is the premium.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (insurance terms)
questions.q: A plan pays 80 percent of the allowed amount after the deductible. The deductible is met and the allowed amount is $200. How much coinsurance does the patient owe?
questions.explain: With 80/20 coinsurance, the plan pays 80 percent and the patient pays 20 percent. Twenty percent of $200 is $40. The $160 is the plan's share, a common mix-up.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (insurance terms)
questions.q: What is an insurance premium?
options: The amount owed by the patient after each visit
The provider's full fee for a service
The amount paid regularly to keep coverage
The refund given for unused benefits
questions.explain: The premium is paid, usually monthly, to keep the policy in force whether or not services are used. Deductibles, copayments and coinsurance are cost sharing for services received.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (claims)
questions.q: What is an explanation of benefits?
options: A bill sent from the provider to the patient
A statement explaining how a claim was paid
A form the patient signs at registration
A list of the provider's fees for services
questions.explain: An explanation of benefits from the insurer shows the amount billed, allowed amount, payment and patient responsibility for a claim. It is not a bill.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (claims)
questions.q: What is a clean claim?
options: A claim for a patient who has no balance due at all
A claim filed on new paper forms
A claim with no errors that can be paid as sent
A claim the insurer has already denied
questions.explain: A clean claim is complete and accurate, so the payer can process it without asking for more information. Clean claims are paid faster and reduce rework.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (compliance)
questions.q: In medical billing, what is upcoding?
options: Reporting a service on the same day it was provided to the patient
Reporting a higher level of service than documented
Reporting the diagnosis before the procedure
Reporting codes from the newest code book
questions.explain: Upcoding means billing for a more complex or expensive service than was performed or documented. It is a form of fraud that can lead to penalties.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (compliance)
questions.q: Billing separately for parts of a procedure that should be reported with one comprehensive code is called what?
questions.explain: Unbundling reports components separately to increase payment when one code describes the whole procedure. Downcoding reports a lower level, and sequencing is the order of codes.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (accounts receivable)
questions.q: What are accounts receivable in a medical practice?
options: Money owed to the practice for services
Money the practice owes its suppliers
Cash kept on hand for small expenses
Payroll taxes the practice must pay
questions.explain: Accounts receivable are amounts owed to the practice by patients and insurers. Money the practice owes others is accounts payable.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (accounts receivable)
questions.q: What does an accounts receivable aging report show?
options: The ages of all the patients seen in the last month
The age of the office's equipment
Insurance plans grouped by member age
Unpaid balances grouped by how long they are due
questions.explain: An aging report sorts outstanding balances by age, such as 30, 60, 90 and over 120 days. Older balances are less likely to be collected and get follow-up first.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (bookkeeping)
questions.q: A participating provider's fee is higher than the insurer's allowed amount. What usually happens to the difference?
options: It is billed to the patient as a remaining balance
It is written off as a contractual adjustment
It is sent to a collection agency
It is added to the next claim
questions.explain: Participating providers agree to accept the allowed amount, so the difference is written off as a contractual adjustment. Billing the patient for it, balance billing, is generally not allowed under the contract.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (bookkeeping)
questions.q: A patient's account shows a credit balance. What does this mean?
options: The patient owes the practice money
The account was sent to collections
More was paid than was owed
questions.explain: A credit balance means payments exceed charges, for example after an overpayment. The practice reviews it and refunds or applies it according to policy.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (bookkeeping)
questions.q: A patient's check is returned by the bank for insufficient funds. How is the account adjusted?
options: The payment stays and the bank owes the practice
The balance is written off as bad debt
The account is closed without a record
The payment is reversed and the balance restored
questions.explain: A returned check means the payment was never received, so it is reversed and the amount is added back to the balance. Many offices also charge a returned-check fee per policy.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (bookkeeping)
questions.q: What is a day sheet in manual bookkeeping?
options: A list of the next day's appointments
A sheet showing staff hours worked
A daily record of charges, payments and adjustments
A log of the day's phone messages
questions.explain: A day sheet, or daily journal, records all charges, payments and adjustments posted that day, providing a running record and helping detect errors.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (bookkeeping)
questions.q: What is a petty cash fund used for?
questions.explain: Petty cash covers small incidental purchases such as postage or minor supplies. Each payment is supported by a receipt or voucher, and the fund is balanced and replenished regularly.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (collections)
questions.q: Which practice is appropriate when telephoning a patient about an overdue balance?
options: Call late in the evening when the patient is most likely to be at home
Leave balance details with any household member
Call at reasonable hours and speak with the responsible party
Call the patient's employer to discuss the bill
questions.explain: Collection calls should be made at reasonable hours, discussed only with the responsible party and conducted respectfully. Sharing balance details with others or employers breaches privacy.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (insurance terms)
questions.q: A child is covered by both parents' health plans. Under the birthday rule, which plan is primary?
options: The plan of the parent who was born in the earlier year
The parent whose birthday falls first in the year
The plan with the lower deductible
The plan that the father holds
questions.explain: Under the birthday rule, the primary plan belongs to the parent whose month and day of birth fall earlier in the calendar year; the birth year is ignored. Custody arrangements can change this.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (insurance terms)
questions.q: When is an Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage given to a Medicare patient?
options: After Medicare has already paid the claim in full
At every visit for every patient
Only when the patient is admitted
Before a service Medicare may not cover
questions.explain: The ABN is given before a service that Medicare may not cover, so the patient can decide whether to receive it and agree to pay if Medicare denies payment.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (records management)
questions.q: What generally determines how long a medical office keeps patient records?
options: The preference the patient states at the very first visit
Federal and state law and the office retention policy
The amount of storage space available
The age of the provider who wrote the notes
questions.explain: Retention periods are set by applicable federal and state laws, payer requirements and the practice's written retention policy, which often keeps minors' records longer.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (records management)
questions.q: When paper medical records reach the end of their retention period, how should they be destroyed?
options: By shredding so the information cannot be read
By placing them in the regular recycling bin
By giving them to the patient's neighbors
By leaving them in a locked car trunk
questions.explain: Records containing protected health information must be destroyed so they cannot be read or reconstructed, such as by shredding, and the destruction is documented.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (coding)
questions.q: What does a CPT modifier indicate?
options: A service was altered by a specific circumstance
A diagnosis is no longer active
A code was deleted from the code set
questions.explain: Modifiers are two-character additions that show a service was changed by a circumstance, such as a bilateral procedure or distinct service, without changing the code's basic definition.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (scheduling)
questions.q: Which scheduling approach groups similar appointments, such as all physicals, into the same block of time?
questions.explain: Cluster, or categorization, scheduling groups similar visit types so equipment and staff are used efficiently. Double booking places two patients in one slot.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (scheduling)
questions.q: An office sees patients in order of arrival during set hours without appointments. What is this called?
questions.explain: Open office hours have no appointments; patients are seen as they arrive during posted hours, as in some walk-in clinics. Wave and stream methods use booked times.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (billing)
questions.q: What is the guarantor on a patient account?
options: The person responsible for paying the bill
The insurer that pays the claim on the account
questions.explain: The guarantor is the person financially responsible for the account, such as a parent for a minor. It is not necessarily the patient or the insurer.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (coding)
questions.q: What do evaluation and management codes in CPT describe?
options: Provider visits such as office visits
questions.explain: Evaluation and management codes report visits and consultations in which providers assess and manage patients. Laboratory, surgery and equipment have their own code sections or code sets.

questions.ref: AAMA CMA content outline, Administrative (billing)
questions.q: What is an encounter form, often called a superbill?
options: A report of the patient's lab results
A letter sent to a patient with a balance
A record of the office's monthly expenses
A form listing a visit's services and diagnoses
questions.explain: The encounter form captures the services, procedures and diagnoses for a visit, along with patient and provider details, and is used to post charges and create the claim.
